evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep jumps straight into probing: 'I just wanna confirm you're moving from a third floor, one bedroom apartment...' — no time-box framing or dependable-quote promise, and no wait for customer buy-in.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics probing without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised by customer to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (third floor, one bedroom), floor/stories (third to second), rooms (one bedroom, no extras), walking distance (30 feet estimated), special items (bed, couch, TV stands, boxes), elevator access (available), additional stops (none mentioned but not explicitly confirmed).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked. Rep discusses boxes but frames it as 'typical box count' for the size, not as an offered service: 'a typical one bedroom apartment usually has fifteen to 25...'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked as typical range: 'a typical one bedroom apartment usually has fifteen to 25' and customer responds with 'Maybe just like a few.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — rep gives range anchored to home size: 'a typical one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours' and personalizes to customer's situation: 'since you are moving from a third floor apartment with elevator access, going to a second floor... your move to be between... two and a half to three and a half hours. So, it's safe to budget around $555 to $777.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — rep discloses all fees upfront: 'no hidden fees of any type, no credit card fees, no deposit, no transportation fees, no stair well fees, no disassemble, reassembly fees' and covers 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments: 'We have a two and a half hour minimum and once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — after giving the estimate, rep immediately pivots to the ask: 'So, it's safe to budget around $555 to $777. So, having that said, would you like our help with your upcoming move on, on Saturday, October 17th.' No 'does that feel fair?' and no silence pause.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full — rep explains discount terms clearly: 'If we can make it in a time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full — rep covers $2,000 limit, no-deductible/no-fine-print framing, and built-in pricing: 'you will have access to the insurance or then no worries damage coverage for up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm that the Two Promises address customer concerns. Moves directly to asking if they want help.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway — rep asks 'for now Kenzie will there be anything else that I can help you with today?' — a generic empty close, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' version.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked — no 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out — rep asks but immediately provides an exit: 'would you like our help with your upcoming move on, on Saturday, October 17th.' Customer says 'Can I just wanted to get a quote today... can I just reach out to you guys if I choose to go through with you?' Rep responds 'Of course, not a problem. Let me will email you all of the information...' — the out was built in and accepted without resistance.

top_strength: Jevic executed thorough logistics probing and gathered all seven detailed items (property type, floor, rooms, walking distance, special items, elevator access, box inventory) with follow-up clarification, creating a solid foundation for an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Section 1 skipped the entire quid-pro-quo framing (no time-box promise, no 'dependable quote' offer, no wait for a yes), and Section 2 never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' — these two absences mean the call missed two of the three highest-leverage moments to set expectations and uncover real deal-drivers before pricing.
